    • paint

      public void paint()
      The `paint()` method is responsible for painting the game screen. It first draws the background image on the canvas. Then, it calls the `paintBoxes()` method to paint the boxes on the screen. It also draws the number of remaining bombs and the number of remaining lives on the screen. Finally, it iterates through the list of enemies, paints them on the screen, and checks for collisions between the avatar and the enemies.
      Specified by:
      paint in class Screen

    • drawNumber

      public void drawNumber(int number, double x, double y)
      The `drawNumber` method is responsible for drawing a number on the game screen. It takes three parameters: `number`, which is the number to be drawn, and `x` and `y`, which are the coordinates where the number should be drawn on the canvas.
      Specified by:

    • drawLifes

      public void drawLifes()
      The `drawLifes()` method is responsible for drawing the remaining lives of the avatar on the game screen. It checks if the `avatar` object has any remaining lives (`getNumLifes()` method), and if so, it iterates through the list of `Life` objects (`avatar.getNumLifes()`) and calls the `paint()` method on each `Life` object to draw it on the screen.
      Specified by:
      drawLifes in class Screen

    • paintBoxes

      public void paintBoxes()
      The `paintBoxes()` method is responsible for painting the boxes on the game screen. It iterates through the list of `Box` objects (`boxes`) and calls the `paintBox()` method on each `Box` object to draw it on the screen. The `paintBox()` method takes an integer parameter (`3`) which determines the size of the box.
      Specified by:
      paintBoxes in class Screen

    • gameOver

      public boolean gameOver() throws IOException
      The `win()` method is checking if the avatar is in the door. If the avatar is in the door, it opens the "goal-view.fxml" scene and returns true. Otherwise, it returns false. The `throws IOException` indicates that the method may throw an IOException if there is an error opening the scene.
